Variables don’t just store values, they make your code dynamic. When used with math operators like +, -, ×, or ÷, they help your program react, calculate, and change as it runs... making it come alive!

The Math-operator block can be used to calculate addition, subtraction, division and multiplication. 



The following shows some examples of how you can change the value of a variable using the Math-operator instead of the Change block.



This is how you set a variable to a random value.
 

You can also plug in the Math-operator block into the LCD block for display but remember to use the Create-text-with block to convert values to text.

Let's practise using the Math-operator block.
1. Create 2 variables x and y.
2. Set them each to a random value from 1 to 9.
3. Using Math-operator block, calculate their total and display the result on the LCD in the format as shown.
    
Recall that a Create-text-with block can multiple values into one row of text.

When solving problems, especially in coding, you don’t always rely on formulas you’ve learned in school. Very often, you’ll need to create your own formulas to tackle unique challenges and situations.

The Math-operator block can be used to calculate addition, subtraction, division and multiplication. 



The following shows some examples of how you can change the value of a variable using the Math-operator instead of the Change block.



This is how you set a variable to a random value.
 

You can also plug in the Math-operator block into the LCD block for display but remember to use the Create-text-with block to convert values to text.

When using multiple Math-operator blocks to create formula, be careful how you place them together. 


You saw this question in a Math homework:
     You have 10 coins. You spend x number of coins 
     and give 2 to a friend. How many do you have left?

x is an unknown number (variable). If x is 1, then answer will be 7. If x is 8, then answer will be 0. To solve it, you can form this formula: 
    10 - (x + 2)

Don't worry if you do not understand the math yet (kudos if you do!). We just want to practise converting the formula into a code.
1. Create a variable x and set it to a random number from 1 to 8.
2. Using Math-operator blocks, create the formula 10 - (x + 2) and display the result in the format as shown.

Use Create-text-with block to join variables and text into one row
